subjective: Oreo, a male Airedale Terrier weighing approximately 7-8 kg, has been experiencing bloody discharge for more than one day, with the previous day showing continuous bleeding. The owner reports a history of digestive issues and episodes of diarrhea and endocrine problems occurring intermittently over the past two months. The symptoms improve 1-2 days after administration of a medication referred to as Intercon, but administration is challenging as Oreo detects medicine mixed in food and refuses to eat. The owner has given two doses of endocrine medication last week. The owner also notes that Oreo tends to lick things during walks, which seems to trigger recurrence of symptoms. The owner is considering giving curd or moistening food to facilitate medication administration.
objective: Blood tests have been performed previously due to digestive issues. No recent ultrasonography (USG) was done as the previous one is considered too old. No new diagnostic tests were performed during this consultation. Physical examination details are not explicitly provided. The owner reports Oreo's weight as 7-8 kg, less than 10 kg. No specific vital signs or physical exam findings were documented.
assessment: Oreo is experiencing recurrent episodes of bloody discharge, digestive disturbances, diarrhea, and endocrine-related issues over the past two months. The symptoms temporarily improve with administration of endocrine medication (Intercon), but medication administration is problematic due to Oreo's refusal to eat medicated food. The recurrent nature and association with licking or environmental exposure during walks suggest possible ongoing irritation or ingestion of irritants. The exact source of bleeding and endocrine issues requires further evaluation. The owner is attempting to manage symptoms with current medication and supportive care.
plan:
Diagnostic: No new diagnostics planned at this time; previous blood tests available; USG not repeated due to owner preference.
Therapeutic: Continue administration of endocrine medication (Intercon) as prescribed; consider moistening food or using curd to facilitate medication administration.
Supportive Care: Advise moistening or softening of food to ease chewing and medication acceptance; monitor for recurrence of symptoms.
Owner Instructions: Encourage owner to continue medication despite administration challenges; try mixing medicine with curd or moist food; observe for any new symptoms or worsening bleeding.
Monitoring: Monitor Oreo's response to medication and symptom recurrence; follow up if bleeding persists or worsens.
No specific follow-up appointment or additional treatments were discussed during this consultation.
conclusion: Oreo, a male Airedale Terrier, has been experiencing intermittent bloody discharge and digestive disturbances over the past two months, with symptoms improving temporarily after endocrine medication administration. Medication administration is challenging due to Oreo's refusal to eat medicated food. No new diagnostics were performed during this consultation. The owner is advised to continue current medication and try moistening food or using curd to facilitate administration. Close monitoring of symptoms and medication response is recommended, with follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen.
key_issues:
1. Recurrent bloody discharge lasting more than one day with intermittent episodes over two months, possibly related to gastrointestinal or endocrine causes.
2. Digestive disturbances including diarrhea and poor digestion.
3. Difficulty in medication administration due to Oreo's refusal to eat medicated food.
abnormal_findings: Persistent bloody discharge noted by owner; history of diarrhea and digestive issues; endocrine-related symptoms as per owner report.
customer_instructions: Continue administering endocrine medication (Intercon) as prescribed. To improve medication acceptance, try mixing medicine with curd or moistening food with water to soften it. Monitor Oreo for any worsening of bleeding or digestive symptoms. Avoid stopping medication abruptly. Observe Oreo's behavior during walks to prevent ingestion of irritants. Contact the veterinarian if symptoms persist or worsen.
reminders: Monitor Oreo's symptoms closely and follow up if bleeding continues or worsens. No specific follow-up appointment was scheduled during this consultation.
